transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Harbor Head of ML), Ethan Li (Harbor Platform), Lena Ortiz (Harbor SecOps), Tom Bianchi (Harbor SRE)

Summary: Quick demo of model catalog and how to read bench signals + deployment path recommendations. Focus on small set of open models, interpreting p95/p99, and mapping to hosted/dedicated/private.

Topics covered: model selection heuristics, bench configs, compatibility matrix, routing/fallbacks, quantization tradeoffs, KV/prefix cache, security questions (SOC2/KMS), and next steps for pilot.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Maya (Redwood): ok everyone thanks for joining; i'm maya, i'll run the demo and diego will jump into the benchmark bits. can you all see my screen?
00:08 Priya (Harbor): yes got it, looks good, thanks.
00:12 Diego (Redwood SE): hey hi, quick agenda: catalog walk, bench primer, compatibility matrix, then q&a and next steps. we'll try to keep it tight.
00:22 Ethan (Harbor): great, we're interested in how you pick open models for customer workloads and specifically the latency vs cost guidance. our prod traffic is a mix of short prompts (customer messages) and long-context analytics queries.
00:34 Maya: perfect, that's exactly what we'll map to today. starting with the catalog filter - note we tag models by use-case and by kernel compat. sometimes the auto-detected kernels are off, you'll see that in a sec.
00:48 Asha (Redwood): quick note — our compatibility matrix includes recommended quant levels (8-bit, 4-bit experimental), and whether the model supports persistent kv cache. the sheet we export has a column called "k v cache" sometimes transcribed as kvk — sorry the fireflies auto text is messy.
01:05 Priya: no worries, that's fine. can you show a short example?
01:10 Diego: yep. (screen) here is a shortlisting workflow — we take perf bench signals: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency for a 32-token response, and a synthetic eval for quality. benchmark config matters — batch sizes, seq len, and prompt templates.
01:34 Diego: for Harbor's short prompts we'd look at p95 at 16 tokens and throughput at small batch sizes. for analytical queries we look at 512+ seq lengths and memory/k v usage.
02:02 Tom (Harbor): when you say k v usage do you mean the persistent prefix cache that stores key/value states between calls? we've tried a naive cache and saw evictions.
02:12 Asha: yep, persistent prefix/KV cache — it's tricky across sharded setups. we recommend affinity routing and sticky kernels for low-eviction workloads. if you have multi-tenant pins, that's where dedicated helps.
02:28 Priya: is there a hard number for latency we can expect on hosted? 90th percentile ideally under 120ms for small prompts.
02:36 Maya: for hosted, depends on model. for a smaller open model we've seen p90 ~80-140ms on our smallest dedicated hosts, hosted tier varies but you can expect somewhere in that band; with batching and cache it improves. for production you'd probably go dedicated to hit consistent p90 targets.
03:00 Ethan: and cost delta between hosted and dedicated? our finance team will want ballpark.
03:06 Maya: ballpark example: hosted per-token is easier to start — but dedicated commit reduces unit cost by ~30-50% depending on utilization. we'll send a tailored pricing estimate.
03:18 Priya: ok good. show us the bench spreadsheet and how to interpret weird signals, like when quality and latency disagree.
03:25 Diego: right — (opens sheet) here's a real bench. you'll see a model with low latency but quality drop on our eval prompts. that's often due to quantization or kernel mismatch. we flag that in the matrix as "quality risk".
03:40 Diego: also note the kernel mapping: sometimes our compile picks a cu-optimized kernel that degrades long-context perf; we add a column for "recommended kernel override" you can try.
03:55 Ethan: are kernel overrides something we can control in private deployments?
04:00 Asha: yes, on private you get the control plane and can pin kernels, but on hosted we do safe rollouts and expose toggles via the console.
04:12 Lena (Harbor SecOps): security: SOC2 is table stakes, we also need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for token access.
04:20 Maya: understood. we are SOC2 and we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in our Private and Dedicated offerings. we'll attach the security pack after call.
04:33 Priya: any differences in data residency between hosted and private?
04:37 Maya: hosted has regional endpoints and retention settings; Private gives you full VPC and on-prem option for strict residency.
04:46 Ethan: about benches — what's a good pilot footprint? we don't want full load yet.
04:52 Diego: typical pilot: 2 models, short and long prompt profiles, 2 runs each (peak vs steady) — that gives p50/p95/p99 and token cost estimates. run time per bench depends on workload but usually 1-2 hours per run.
05:12 Tom: can you do a bench that shows prefix cache hit ratio and how that affects per-token cost?
05:18 Diego: yes, we'll include cache-hit metrics and a synthetic with and without prefix cache. also we'll surface KV evictions per window.
05:28 Priya: good. what about fallback routing — we want graceful degradation if dedicated pool saturates.
05:34 Asha: we have routing policies: primary dedicated, fallback to hosted compatible variant, and we can set latency or cost thresholds to trigger fallback. there's also model variant mapping in the compatibility matrix.
05:48 Ethan: ok, show the console view for routing and rollouts.
05:52 Maya: (screen) console -> routing -> policies. you can create canaries, set percent traffic, and automatic fallback. note the trace view ties back to token-level cost.
06:10 Priya: there was a mention of quantization impacting hallucinations — can you show the quality delta?
06:18 Diego: yes here — (shows plot) 4-bit quant improved throughput but quality score drops on long-context summarization. we mark that as a conditional recommendation: for high-quality tasks stick to 8-bit or fp16. quant is model and workload dependent.
06:36 Priya: interesting. do you provide a recommended quant profile per model in the catalog?
06:40 Asha: yes, catalog entries include suggested quant profiles and an "expected quality delta" note from bench runs. sometimes it's experimental.
06:48 Tom: if we do private on-prem, do you support HSM for keys and an air-gapped mode?
06:55 Maya: yes, Private supports HSM and an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments; we'll share the ops checklist.
07:06 Ethan: what about rate limiting and per-route quotas? we need per-customer throttles.
07:12 Diego: console supports per-route quotas and token-based rate limits, and we emit traces so you can correlate to billing.
07:20 Priya: ok can we look at an example bench output for an open model you recommend?
07:25 Diego: sure — here's model "open-phi-7b" (example). bench shows p50 45ms, p95 180ms at 32 token response on hosted; on dedicated with affinity it drops to p95 110ms. quality on your domain eval is 0.87 vs baseline 0.92 for a larger model.
07:52 Priya: so to hit 120ms p95 at scale we'd pick dedicated and leverage prefix cache for repeated short prompts?
07:59 Diego: yes that's the pattern. also consider a smaller model family for cost, with fallback to a larger model when quality regresses.
08:12 Ethan: noted. any non-obvious gotchas?
08:15 Asha: kernel mismatches, collation of kv across shards, and wrong batch config are common. our bench template includes guard rails to avoid those.
08:26 Priya: ok what will you send us after this call?
08:29 Maya: bench config, security pack (SOC2, KMS notes), pricing ranges, and a short slide on cache behavior and routing.
08:38 Tom: perfect. can we tentatively plan bench runs for next week?
08:41 Ethan: i'll sync with infra and confirm by tomorrow.
08:45 Priya: timeline from our side: goal is a production pilot in Q1, need to get security clearance first.
08:51 Maya: understood. we'll prioritize the security docs.
09:00 Diego: quick micro-demo — here's the compatibility matrix filter: you can filter for kernel compat, quant profile, and whether model is "kv-friendly". i can export CSV for you.
09:18 Priya: export would be great. also include notes where we've seen quality regressions.
09:22 Diego: will do.
09:26 Asha: one more note — when we recommend dedicated we also suggest warmup scripts for the cache to reduce cold-start p95 during traffic spikes.
09:38 Priya: good point. how much warmup traffic do you typically need?
09:42 Diego: depends on your active context size; for repeat short prompts a small synthetic of a few thousand tokens can warm the cache. we'll size it for Harbor's profile.
09:55 Ethan: circling back to cost — can you show an example per-route token breakdown in the console?
10:02 Maya: (screen) route analytics -> per-token COST -> you can slice by model and endpoint. you can also set alerts on cost-per-token thresholds.
10:18 Lena: regarding audit logs, can we get raw request logs for a month and tokenized redaction?
10:24 Maya: yes, Private gives you full audit logs and we support token redaction options and retention policy config. we'll include details in the security pack.
10:35 Priya: ok i'm happy with the plan. let's recap next steps.
10:40 Maya: recap: Diego will prepare bench configs and CSV export; Maya will share security docs and pricing; Asha will make a short cache/rollback slide; Ethan will confirm bench windows; Harbor aims to confirm pilot timeline by 2026-12-23.
10:58 Priya: confirmed, thanks everyone.
11:02 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments and a calendar for bench runs. bye.

--- End transcript ---

Notes: transcription contains some auto-misspellings (k v, quand for quant). There is minor crosstalk around 02:00-03:00. Customer requested security pack and two bench runs.
